🟠 **Important**

**Light-theme ghost buttons lose their explicit text color (Delete plugin button turns blue)**

`:root:not(.dark) .btn-ghost[class]` (specificity 0,4,0) forces `color: #0058c2` on every `.btn-ghost` in light mode, and it beats single-class utilities such as `.text-red-400`. `apps/desktop/src/ui/plugins-smart.js:140` renders the destructive `Delete` button as `btn-ghost text-2xs text-red-400`, so in light mode it renders as a blue link-like button instead of red. Any other `btn-ghost` that carries a semantic text color class will be recolored the same way. Scope the override to the ghost buttons that should be blue (e.g. a dedicated class or `:not([class*="text-"])`), or exclude the danger variant explicitly.

This return then leaves the previous label's text and position visible. Clear the visible tooltip and `current` before returning. Keep the existing display path for clipped labels.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Keep narrow-window drags from reflowing page content.** At a narrow width, `onMove` sets `sidebar-expanded` but does not set `sidebar-overlay`. The collapsed offset rule in `styles.css` applies only with `sidebar-overlay`. No other rule preserves that offset while `sidebar-dragging` is active. So the nav width follows the drag position in flow, and the page content moves with the pointer until release. When the drag starts in narrow mode, the overlay state must match the rule `apply()` uses. The sidebar must overlay the content during the move, as the narrow-window behavior requires. The content then returns to its settled layout on release without a jump.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Keep the sidebar shortcut active after the connection detail dialog closes.** After a connection detail dialog closes, its panel remains in `#conn-detail-bg` with `aria-modal="true"`. The `shortcutBelongsElsewhere` predicate counts that panel as an open dialog, so the sidebar shortcut stays disabled. The predicate checks only each modal element's own `hidden` marker and does not see the hidden container. Closed dialogs must not block the shortcut. Choose one fix: - Clear `bg.innerHTML` after the hide timer runs in `dismiss`, or - Make the predicate ignore modal elements that are hidden by an ancestor. Either fix must keep an open connection detail dialog blocking the shortcut.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Pin the drag width before the narrow-window overlay is applied.** In a narrow window, `onDown` adds `sidebar-overlay` before `--sidebar-drag-w` is set. A collapsed sidebar then receives the negative margin `calc(var(--sidebar-w-collapsed) - var(--sidebar-w-expanded))` while its width remains collapsed. The adjacent content shifts on the press, before any drag movement. This conflicts with the overlay's purpose of not reflowing the page under the pointer. Set the drag width from the current width first. The margin then resolves to zero for the collapsed state.
Suggested fix

```diff --- "a/apps/desktop/src/ui/sidebar.js" +++ "b/apps/desktop/src/ui/sidebar.js" @@ -178,9 +178,13 @@ }; edge.setPointerCapture?.(e.pointerId); root.classList.add('sidebar-dragging'); // In a narrow window the sidebar overlays the content while dragged, // so the page does not reflow under the pointer. - if (isNarrow()) root.classList.add('sidebar-overlay'); + if (isNarrow()) { + // Pin the current width first so the overlay margin does not shift the content. + nav.style.setProperty('--sidebar-drag-w', `${drag.startW}px`); + root.classList.add('sidebar-overlay'); + } }; /** @param {PointerEvent} e */ const onMove = (e) => { ```
Committable suggestion

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion if (isNarrow()) { // Pin the current width first so the overlay margin does not shift the content. nav.style.setProperty('--sidebar-drag-w', `${drag.startW}px`); root.classList.add('sidebar-overlay'); } ```
